  "text": "Mara pulled against the woman’s grip. The voice behind the gate laughed, and she stopped. She had never heard herself laugh like that.

The bell swung higher. Each time it passed overhead, the water at their feet rose a little, then fell. On the third swing, a small handprint appeared beside the two dark marks.

“That wasn’t there before,” the harbor master said.

The man from the boat crouched at the quay’s edge. He reached into the water and drew out a photograph, soaked but unblurred. Mara saw three children standing before the gate: the man, the woman, and a girl with Mara’s face.

She looked up. The woman had let go of her wrist.

“How old is this?” Mara asked.

“Older than you,” the woman said.

From behind the iron came the sound of bare feet crossing stone. The lock twitched beneath the woman’s bloodied thumbprint. She pressed her hand to it again, but the bolt had begun to slide.

The harbor master wedged his pole through the gate’s handles. Wood bent. Mara took the photograph from the man and turned it over. On the back, in a child’s cramped writing, were four names. The last had been crossed out so hard the paper had torn.

Through the tear, Mara could see a sliver of movement on the other side of the gate. An eye lowered to the opening.

The voice spoke again, close enough that she felt its breath on her fingers.

“Read the name,” it said."
